justification: Read-only measurement only: three new ledger probes (DQ-143/144/145), three outreach claims declared false, a per-prompt banner line, a committed chapter-scope data file and its tests. Nothing served to a user changes and nothing is written to the database. Standard rather than Minor because six files change and the outreach gate's verdict changes from 16/17 to 16/20.

pre_impl.existing_data: Measured on production before writing: 25,455 served rules; citation_status proven 11,151; part-of-council chapters ungated 510; mixed/unclear/no-chapter ungated 3,756. The chapter scope came from the served-answer audit's checked proposals (235 chapters, 221 quotes found in the PDF by script).
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: The plan said 584 wrong-house rules were left. The whole-gap query found the step-5 chapters were never measured (2,963 + 285 + 508), only 16 of 94 AI 'whole council' labels carry a sentence a fixed pattern confirms, and 630 heritage-area rules carry only a generic heritage tag that reaches every heritage property. Real figures: DQ-143 1,114, DQ-144 8,694 (upper bound). Also found: heritage_precinct_mapping, read by lib/precinct-service.ts, does not exist in production.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: No new tracker: rows go into the existing ledger (dq_probe_live.py PROBES, dq_checks.json, DATA_QUALITY_TRACKER.md) and the existing per-prompt hook live-numbers.py. DQ-142 was already taken, so the plan's 'DQ-142' is DQ-143/144 here.

falsifiable_check.command: python -m pytest tests/test_chapter_scope_probes.py -q ; python scripts/dq_probe_live.py --id DQ-143
falsifiable_check.fails_when: The tests fail if the chapter-scope file is missing or empty (which would make DQ-143 read 0), if the fixed council-wide pattern accepts the C-B 4.4 heritage-vicinity sentence, or if an AI whole-council label alone is enough to clear a chapter. DQ-143 exits 1 while any part-of-council rule is ungated.
falsifiable_check.observed_red: The suite failed 2 of 5 on first run because the council-wide pattern had been written with a literal backspace instead of a word boundary (DQ-144 then read 8,990). Cross-review then found four faults, all fixed: a missing scope file now raises (tested), a heritage-area chapter needs its own area slug (generic tag no longer counts; DQ-143 510 -> 1,114), mapped wording ('shown on Map 1') never confirms whole-council (tested), and the banner labels its sum as non-distinct. A zone subset test was tried and dropped: it read 1,064 false faults because chapter zones are in old codes. 8 of 8 tests pass; the three probes exit 1 as declared open.

functions.name: _chapter_scope_keys
functions.input: filters on part_of_council, applies_to and machine confirmation
functions.output: The council__chapter keys read from data/chapter_scope/chapter_scope_2026-10-11.json that match every filter given
functions.if_none: _load_chapter_scope raises if the file is missing, malformed or empty, so no probe can read 0 for want of data; test_missing_scope_file_raises_not_zero covers it.

values.what: DQ-143 / DQ-144 / DQ-145 readings on production
values.read_at: Read live from production on 2026-10-11 by the probes themselves; the banner re-reads them every ten minutes.
values.if_missing: An unreachable database exits 2 (UNKNOWN), never 0; the banner prints UNKNOWN and the TOTAL becomes UNKNOWN.

queries.purpose: Count served rules that reach every house in their council although their chapter covers only part of it.
queries.where_clause: is_current AND v2_is_actionable AND not TOC AND no precinct gate AND not condition layer AND not heritage-tagged AND zones NULL/empty/ALL AND chapter key in the part-of-council list

break_it.scenario: The chapter-scope data file is deleted or renamed, so the key lists come back empty.
break_it.what_happens: DQ-143 would read 0 and the outreach claim would look met.
break_it.how: test_scope_file_loads_every_chapter asserts 235 keys and test_dq143_has_part_of_council_chapters asserts a known chapter is present.

break_it.scenario: An AI reader labels a local chapter whole-council, hiding it from DQ-144.
break_it.what_happens: Rules for one area would be counted as decided and shown to every house.
break_it.how: A whole-council label counts only when the chapter's own sentence matches the fixed _COUNCIL_WIDE pattern; test_dq144_excludes_only_decided_chapters keeps C-B 4.4 counted.

break_it.scenario: The probe's ungated predicate is narrower than the serving route, so rules that are served are not counted.
break_it.what_happens: The count would understate the wrong-house problem.
break_it.how: Recorded as a scope limit: heritage-tagged rows still reach every heritage house; the predicate mirrors queryLayer in for-property/route.ts as of 2940d1e5. The machine served-answer re-check (step 7) is the end-to-end test.

break_it.scenario: A heritage-area chapter's rules carry a generic heritage tag, so the old predicate treated them as gated.
break_it.what_happens: Rules for one named heritage area reach every heritage property in the council while DQ-143 reads clean.

post_merge.manual_verify: Verified in-session: the three probes, dq_check.py --id for each (consistent with declared open), --coverage OK (147 rows), --outreach 16 of 20 with 0 contradicted. The banner prints the scoreboard.
